messages:
sara: observability-bot just triggered an alert — large S3 multipart upload from service account `svc-reporting-crossenv` to s3://redwood-exports-prod-eu, ~120GB in 6m. Can someone pick this up?
observability-bot: Alert: export_bulk_upload_detected | src=s3 | size_bytes=128345678912 | user=svc-reporting-crossenv | ts=1799123456
ben: I'm on it. @raj @emma FYI — hold any manual containment until we confirm scope.
raj: copying logs now. Quick question: is that service account allowed cross-account exports? I thought it was restricted to staging.
emma: it shouldn't be able to hit prod buckets. svc-reporting-crossenv was added in Jan for a temporary partner job, but I thought we scoped it to staging only. digging into IAM role bindings.
ben: can you paste the audit log lines? also check KMS key usage (alias/redwood-exports).
emma: paste from cloud audit -> ```{"protoPayload": {"authenticationInfo": {"principalEmail": "svc-reporting-crossenv@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"},"serviceName": "s3.amazonaws.com","methodName": "PutObject","requestMetadata": {"callerIp": "54.72.11.23"}},"resourceName": "projects/_/buckets/redwood-exports-prod-eu/objects/2026-03-15/report_2026_03_15.tar"}```
raj: confirmed KMS key `alias/redwood-exports` has decrypt events by that SA at ~1799123452. Key policy allows the reporting role to use it.
security-oncall: recommended immediate containment: 1) disable the service account keys, 2) add deny on S3 PutObject for that role, 3) snapshot the bucket and isolate the objects.
ben: done step 1 (disabled key). infra-bot queueing deny policy update.
infra-bot: Policy change requested -> deny s3:PutObject for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-reporting-crossenv — status: applied (1799123470)
emma: running a scan for other objects uploaded by that SA. so far found 3 objects (the tar + 2 manifests). Listing IPs shows origin IP 54.72.11.23 (we think it's partner CI).
raj: check partner job triggers — there's a CI pipeline that was mis-pointed at prod. ticket #SEC-2026-089 opened. We should also rotate the KMS key access or add a key policy restricting to specific VPC endpoints.
ben: agree. Immediate actions: (A) confirm no exfil to external account (cross-account copies) (B) revoke SA until pipeline fixed (C) preserve logs for forensics.
sara: I'll draft a short comms to data-privacy and compliance: "Potential unauthorized export to prod bucket by mis-scoped service account. Contained — keys disabled, put denied. Investigating partner CI. Ticket SEC-2026-089."
security-oncall: post-incident items: 1) tighten RBAC on reporting roles, 2) add CI job guardrails (env checks), 3) KMS policy to restrict decrypt to requests from our VPC endpoints, 4) add an audit alert for service accounts performing >10GB uploads in 10m.
emma: note for root cause: team accidentally re-applied terraform workspace variables from staging to prod during onboarding. we'll add a preflight check to the infra templates.
ben: forensics note: snapshot the three uploaded objects and copy to secure forensic bucket (do not delete live objects until compliance signs off).
sara: thanks all. i'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. assigning owners: RBAC audit = emma, KMS policy = raj, CI guards = devops team (cc @devops). leaving this thread open until postmortem doc is linked.
